subject: Meadowlane SLO confirmation and POC next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Cheng <laura@meadowlane.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T15:02:00Z
Subject: Meadowlane SLO confirmation and POC next steps

Hi Laura — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything aligned before we schedule the POC: 

What we heard (please confirm):
- Target 95th pct latency: <= 350 ms for typical requests up to ~512 input tokens (text generation path).
- Streaming requirement: token-chunk latency tail <= 200 ms (end-to-end chunk to client) for customer streaming sessions.
- Sustained throughput: 120 requests/sec (steady state).
- Concurrency: up to 30 simultaneous streaming sessions during peak.
- Availability target: 99.5% during business hours (Mon–Fri 8am–8pm PT).

Attachments: I attached a lightweight SLO checklist (meadowlane-slo-checklist.xlsx) and a draft Mutual Action Plan (mutual-action-plan.md) with the milestone dates we sketched in the call.

Ask from you: can you confirm the traffic shape for the next 30 days (we only need a simple CSV with per-hour request counts and average payload size) and provide sample request payloads (anonymized) for both the streaming and non-streaming flows. That will let our infra and bench team size the POC and pre-select capacity profiles.

Proposed POC outline (high level):
- Duration: 2 weeks (bench + validation).
- Goal: demonstrate 95th <= 350 ms at 512 tokens with concurrency 30 and sustain 120 rps for a 30-minute soak.
- Deliverables: bench report (latency percentiles), streaming chunk latency plot, ops runbook for failover/fallback, and recommendation for Dedicated vs Hosted config.
- Start window: earliest week of Dec 14 — we can finalize calendar once you confirm sample data and access.

Next steps (for both teams):
- Laura: share traffic CSV and sample payloads, confirm POC start window.
- Redwood: we'll prepare POC runbook and allocate bench GPUs; Ben and Soojin will own execution.

Thanks — I’ll sync with Ben and Soojin today and share a more detailed runbook.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Attachments: meadowlane-slo-checklist.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.md
From: Laura Cheng <laura@meadowlane.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T14:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Meadowlane SLO confirmation and POC next steps

Thanks Marcus — that matches what we discussed. A couple of clarifications and the traffic export attached.

Clarifications:
- The 120 rps target is for the inference endpoint only (we have a separate pre-processing cluster). Peak is usually a 2-hour window each business day, with short spikes up to ~150 rps for under 10 minutes.
- For streaming, chunk sizes vary; typical token bursts are ~20–40 tokens per chunk. About 80% of sessions use streaming.
- Payload sizes: average input tokens ~220, average output target length ~140 tokens.

Attached: meadowlane-traffic.csv (hourly counts for the past 30 days) and a sanitized sample request for streaming.

One more ask: can you confirm whether the POC will run in our AWS account (preferred) or in Redwood’s hosted environment? We prefer to test in our account to validate network egress and VPC routing.

Also — what is the typical cost delta if we ask Redwood to reserve a small Dedicated pool for the POC? We need to budget for it before the internal sign-off.

Laura Cheng
Head of Data Products | Meadowlane Analytics
laura@meadowlane.io
Attachments: meadowlane-traffic.csv, sample_streaming_payload.json
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Cheng <laura@meadowlane.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Meadowlane SLO confirmation and POC next steps

Laura — great, thanks for the traffic export and the sample payload. We reviewed the CSV and a proposed plan is below.

Short answers:
- POC location: we can run either in your AWS account (preferred for network validation) or in Redwood hosted. For your VPC routing and egress validation, running in your account with our Private agent is the right choice.
- Cost for short Dedicated allocation: for a 2-week POC we typically recommend a small dedicated pool (equivalent to 2 x A100-class GPUs or 3 x H100 small nodes depending on model family) — rough indicative lift: $5k–$8k for reserved short-term capacity (we’ll provide a precise quote once we pick exact instance types).

Proposed POC runbook (summary):
- Week 0 (prep): access & IAM, sample datasets, schedule bench windows.
- Week 1 (benching): staged load tests to validate latency percentiles at 512 tokens across single-node and multi-node configs; streaming chunk latency monitored at 1ms granularity; ramp to 120 rps sustained and inject 150 rps 10-min spike test.
- Week 2 (validation + soak): run 30-min soak at target concurrency (30 streaming sessions) and gather operational metrics; run failover scenarios (region fallback + reduced capacity).

Success criteria (pass/fail style):
- 95th latency <= 350 ms for generation path at 512 tokens.
- Streaming chunk tail <= 200 ms for 95th percentile of chunks.
- No errors above 0.5% during soak.
- Acceptable model output quality regression < 2% on your evaluation prompts (we'll run a quick eval set you provide).

Deliverables: detailed bench report, ops runbook (poc-runbook.pdf), recommended runtime config (batching/quantization settings), and a cost estimate for a production Dedicated pool.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Laura (by 2026-12-09): confirm POC start week and share AWS account role for Redwood agent.
- Redwood (Ben & Soojin) (by 2026-12-10): deliver final POC runbook and quote for Dedicated lift.
- Marcus: schedule kickoff meeting once access is provided.

We attached our draft POC runbook to this message for your review (poc-runbook.pdf). If that looks good, we can lock the calendar for Dec 15 start.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachments: poc-runbook.pdf
From: Laura Cheng <laura@meadowlane.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T16:30:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Meadowlane SLO confirmation and POC next steps

Thanks Ben — Dec 15 works for us. We'll provision an IAM role for Redwood and share the details by EOD Dec 9.

Regarding cost: that $5k–$8k range is reasonable for the POC. I'll share the budget note with procurement and confirm.

One other item — our security team asked whether you'll be able to provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and a data retention / deletion plan for the POC. Happy to loop them in if needed.

Laura
Head of Data Products | Meadowlane Analytics
